title: teamrig config
description: Team settings for the teamrig plugin. Only the roster (sessions, roles.lead) is required; every other key has a default. Unknown keys are kept as they are.

$schema.description: The JSON schema this file follows, for an editor's completion and checks.

configVersion.description: The config format. The CLI migrates older files and refuses to write newer ones.

team.description: Where the team sits in a tree of teams. A team with no parent is the root of its own tree. teamrig team create writes it.

id.description: The team's id: the name of its folder under <kit home>/teams/.

parent.description: The parent team: this team's lead reports to that team's lead. A tree has at most 3 levels, and a team at most 8 child teams.

project.description: The team's project folder, an absolute path: where its CLAUDE.md and rule files sit (teamrig check, doctor and rule-conflicts read them there), and where teamrig open starts its sessions unless a session's launch.<id>.project names another. Unset, the folder holding the team's .teamrig.json pointer; doctor flags a folder that does not exist.

sessions.description: Every session id on the team, the lead included. Ids key every file and record, so they never change; a rename only appends to the team's rename log.

names.description: Each session's first display and Claude Code session name, by id. A session not listed is named <team>-<id>. A name must be unique, never another session's id and never one Claude Code keeps for itself (main, team-lead, user, system), since a message to one never reaches a session. A rename in the team's rename log wins over it, and it keeps finding the session.

leads.description: Each sub-lead's members, by id: a sub-lead leads the sessions it lists, and roles.lead every session no sub-lead lists; a sub-lead may list sub-leads, at any depth. A session has one leader, roles.lead is never a member, and no sub-lead leads itself. Written by teamrig promote and demote.

lead.description: Owns priorities, team rules and the owner's decision queue.

deliveryOwner.description: Owns the delivery flow and fleet health, when the team has that role; a child team may leave it to a team above.

securityReviewer.description: Reviews the privileged commands sessions ask to run (exec) and the hand steps they give the human (core rule 11), when the team has that role; the owner always may too. A child team may leave it to a team above.

ownerGates.description: Decision areas only the human owner can approve; silence never counts as consent for them.

ruleConflicts.description: Local rules (a line of a CLAUDE.md, rules file, skill, memory file, hook or settings file) kept although they conflict with a core rule, each with the side that wins. teamrig rules scan finds them; teamrig rules keep records one, teamrig rules forget drops one. The core pack lists them.

file.description: The file, ~/-relative under the user's home folder, else absolute.

text.description: The start of the line's text, which finds the line again when the lines above it move.

rule.description: The core rule it conflicts with, by key; teamrig rules lists them by number.

wins.description: local: the local rule wins over the core rule. teamrig: the core rule wins and the local text stays, which may not always hold (removing the line is safer).

reason.description: Why the user kept it, in their words.

messages.description: Messages between sessions: how long one may be, and when a send to an idle session is held as a cold wake.

maxLines.description: The longest message one session may send another.

coldAfterMinutes.description: Minutes a session may sit idle before a message to it counts as a cold wake (its first call re-reads its whole context at full price). A send to a session idle this long is held once with a note to use an inbox line or send it again; 0 never holds.

register.description: The task list (the register): its priority levels, what each status change needs, its text limits and the thresholds of the flags teamrig check raises on tasks.

ownerSource.description: The --source that marks a task as ordered by the human owner.

priorities.description: The priority levels, most urgent first; a task's priority prints as p<id>. Above them every team has teamrig's own p0, for urgent work done right now, which no config lists. Config version 1 called them tiers.

id.description: The level's number: a task prints it as p<id>, and 1 is the most urgent a config names (0 is teamrig's own p0).

name.description: What the level holds, in a few words.

goalPattern.description: When set, every goal tag on a new task must match this regular expression.

goals.description: How teamrig add and update hold a task's goal tags to the goal records (teamrig goal) of its team and every team above it: free takes any tag; checked refuses a tag that is no such goal record; required also needs an owner-asked or p0/p1 add to name its goal, or --goals none.

maxTitle.description: The most characters a task title may have.

maxText.description: The most characters of a task's other text, such as its ref and notes; the title and the description have their own limits.

secretPatterns.description: Extra regular expressions, matched case-insensitively, that refuse secret-looking text on top of the built-in shapes (vendor tokens, private keys, JSON web tokens, credentials in URLs, password= assignments).

requireDescription.description: Whether teamrig add needs --description, what the task is and why in plain words for a person, and teamrig update refuses --description none. Tasks imported from GitHub take the issue body either way.

requireEvidenceOnDone.description: Whether teamrig set --status done needs --evidence, unless the task already has some.

requireSkillOnDone.description: Whether teamrig set --status done needs --skill: the skill that holds the work's procedure, or none.

requireNoteOn.description: Statuses that cannot be set without a note.

requireFollowupsOn.description: Statuses that cannot be set without --followups: the tasks the work leaves (a finding, a next step), or none.

autoArchive.description: After the first teamrig compact, a write that leaves the task list's log over 512 KiB archives it and says so in a NOTE line. false: only teamrig compact archives it.

requireDecisionCard.description: Whether teamrig set --status waiting on the owner's decision or approval needs a decision card (--question, --options, --recommend, --default), so the owner decides from it alone.

requireProofOnVerifying.description: Whether teamrig set --status verifying needs --proof, what will prove the shipped change works, and --waits naming when it runs: a time, or a task in progress or verifying.

verifyGate.description: teamrig set --status in-progress while a task it needs (--after, or --waits task:) is verifying: refuse it, or warn and start it. Either way the verifying task's owner gets one inbox line a day about it.

maxVerifying.description: A session holding more verifying tasks than this is a PILE-UP in teamrig check; 0 turns the flag off.

maxReparks.description: How many times in a row a verifying task's proof may be put off to other waits; past it teamrig set --status verifying with other waits is refused and teamrig check flags REPARKED. 0 turns both off.

check.description: The thresholds of the flags teamrig check raises on tasks.

staleAfterHours.description: An active task untouched this long is STALE.

notPickedUpAfterHours.description: An open task its owner has not touched this long after it was assigned is NOT-PICKED-UP.

prioritySkipAfterHours.description: A session's in-progress task outranked this long by its own open task, on band and score, is a PRIORITY-SKIP.

maxSelfMadePerDay.description: A session that added more tasks for itself (created by it, asked by no one else) in the last 24 hours than this is a SELF-MADE in teamrig check; 0 turns the flag off.

goalProgressDays.description: Whole days (the team's day: wake.dayStartUtc, else UTC) that may end with no goal or week-plan task moved by its owner, while the week has usage left, before a NO-PROGRESS in teamrig check; 0 turns the flag off.

overSizeMultiple.description: An active sized task whose cost since it was last sized, as the budget meter attributes it, passed this many times its size (--size) is OVER-SIZE in teamrig check; 0 turns the flag off.

weekLengthDays.description: The length, in days, of the week plan teamrig check measures the week's tasks against.

stopgapFiles.description: The files teamrig check scans for stopgap T<id> tags besides every skill, a STOPGAP-DONE flag for each tag that names a finished task: paths relative to the team's project folder, or absolute; a path ending in .md is one file, any other a folder whose .md files are read.

review.description: How teamrig asks for a bug's review.

mode.description: A bug (--type bug) reaching a requireOn status with review parts missing (--cause, --how, --prevent, --missed-test, --missed-monitor, --missed-log, and --harden when critical): refuse the change and name the missing flags, warn (make it and print them), or off (ask nothing).

requireOn.description: The statuses a bug cannot reach with review parts missing. A dropped task is never asked: its note says why.

criticalOwners.description: Sessions whose every bug counts as critical, and so is asked --harden too: a team's security or data areas.

hintPattern.description: A regular expression, matched case-insensitively against the title and description of a task with no type: a match prints a NOTE line asking to mark it --type bug [--critical], or --type task, when the task is added and when it starts.

skills.description: The team's Claude Code skills: the shared area prefix, the limits teamrig check holds each skill to, and how a session lists the skills of other areas.

sharedPrefix.description: The area prefix of skills shared by the whole team.

maxDescriptionWords.description: A skill whose description runs over this many words is flagged DESCRIPTION.

maxPerArea.description: An area with more skills than this is flagged AREA-OVER-LIMIT: merge before adding.

maxVerifiedAgeDays.description: A skill last verified more than this many days ago is flagged UNVERIFIED.

forbidFrontmatter.description: Frontmatter keys a team skill may not set; a skill is never a permission.

otherAreas.description: How a session teamrig launches lists a skill of another session's area whose "Used by:" line does not name it: on in full, name-only without its description, user-invocable-only only as a /name command the model is not shown, off not at all. Shared and personal skills are always listed in full.

contextFiles.description: Character budgets for the text Claude Code puts in every call's context; teamrig doctor flags a file over its budget.

maxClaudeMdChars.description: The CLAUDE.md files a session loads: the user's, and the project folder's and each parent's.

maxSkillListingChars.description: The skill listing: one name: description line per skill.

maxSessionListsChars.description: The lists the newest session's context holds: skills, deferred tools, agent types and MCP server instructions.

lock.description: The file lock each write of the team's state files takes (the task list, the exec audit, the GitHub sync), so two writes never interleave.

ttlMs.description: The longest, in ms, a holder keeps a lock: one older than this is taken over even while a process with its pid runs, since that pid may be another process's by then. A lock whose process is gone is taken over at once.

pollMs.description: How often, in ms, a waiter retries.

waitMs.description: How long, in ms, a waiter tries before it gives up.

pushGuard.description: The push guard: what a git push to a protected branch does.

protectedBranches.description: The branches the push guard watches: a push to one goes as pushToProtected says; force-push, mirror and deletion are refused. An empty list guards nothing.

pushToProtected.description: A normal push to a protected branch: ask asks the human, allow lets it through with a note, lead lets the lead's own through and another session's once the lead approved its waiting task (teamrig approve), else refuses it with how to ask, never asking the human. gated clears a hand push as lead does, and teamrig merge merges a change that holds the self-merge gates (its own live task, a pass record of the rebased tree, commit sizes, tests with source, the repo's review gate) with no approval, logging it in merges.jsonl, and holds one that misses a gate for its session's leader. Force-push, mirror and deletion stay refused; a --force-with-lease push and a command the guard cannot read still ask.

reviewPaths.description: The team's review gate entries, read on top of teamrig's generic security list (lockfiles, package manager config, git and agent hooks, CI, container files, git attributes), which none removes. A glob with no slash names a file at any depth, one with a slash is read from the repo root; case is ignored. always holds a change touching the path for its class's reviewer; check runs the repo's reviewCheck first. A bad mode or class reads as always and security.

glob.description: The paths the entry covers: with no slash a file name at any depth, with one a path from the repo root; case is ignored.

mode.description: always holds a change touching the paths for the class's reviewer; check runs the repo's reviewCheck first, which clears the change or holds it.

class.description: Who reviews a held change: security (roles.securityReviewer), or leader (the session's lead or sub-lead).

exec.description: Privileged commands a reviewer approved, run once by teamrig exec run.

path.description: The folders a privileged command's bare program name (teamrig exec) is looked up on, in order, and the only PATH its commands get; the session's own PATH is never searched. Each is absolute (C:/tools, /usr/bin) with no ; or : past the drive. Empty: a request names its program by absolute path.

webhookEnv.description: The name of the environment variable holding the webhook URL that every exec approval, refusal and run is posted to, never the URL itself. Absent: nothing is posted; named but unset: each would-be post warns.

packageGuard.description: The package guard: what a Bash or PowerShell call that installs a package or runs one ad hoc does.

adHocRunners.description: A Bash or PowerShell call that fetches a package outside the project's lockfile and runs it at once (npx of a tool not in node_modules/.bin, npm exec, npm create or init <x>, pnpm dlx, yarn dlx, bunx): deny refuses it, ask asks the human, allow lets it run.

installs.description: A Bash or PowerShell call that installs a package version the guard cannot vet (npm install, pnpm add, yarn add, bun add and their updates): a range or a bare update rather than an exact version or tag, a git or URL source, or a version published fewer than cooldownDays ago or with a known advisory. deny refuses it, ask asks the human, allow lets it run.

cooldownDays.description: A version published fewer days ago than this is not vetted: a fresh release is unproven. 0 vets any age.

commitGuard.description: The commit guard: what a Bash or PowerShell call that runs git without the repository's hooks does.

skipHooks.description: A Bash or PowerShell call that runs git without the repository's hooks: --no-verify (or -n for git commit and git am), HUSKY set for it, or a core.hooksPath that -c, a GIT_CONFIG* variable or git config sets or unsets: deny refuses it, ask asks the human, allow lets it run.

prompts.description: The permission prompts teamrig's own hooks raise.

hookAsks.description: A call a teamrig hook would ask the human about (a push to a protected branch or one it cannot read, an ad-hoc package run, a git command without hooks, a call that would print a secret, a helper over the budget, as their own keys set): ask raises the permission prompt; refuse refuses it instead, its reason telling the session to record the step as waiting for the owner's approval and take its next task, so no prompt holds a session while nobody is there to answer it.

routeAllow.description: While hookAsks is refuse: on lets a Bash line that runs a sanctioned route marked for it (teamrig merge, deploy, exec request, worktree remove, git commit) run with no permission check at all, once every teamrig guard passed it, logged by its route alone; off takes that allow away without a release. It only takes allows away: no config adds a route. Inert while hookAsks is ask.

secretGuard.description: Refuses a Bash, PowerShell, Read or Grep call that would print a secret into the session, where it stays in the transcript and every later prompt: a secret file's content, the whole environment, a secret variable's value, a Kubernetes secret's data or a dump command's output (kubectl config view --raw); and a Bash or PowerShell line that holds a secret as text (a token, credentials in a URL or an Authorization header), as the line itself stays in the transcript; and a Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit whose written text holds one, unless it writes a secret file (paths). A value handed to the tool that needs it (a pipe into docker login --password-stdin, a redirect into a file) stays allowed, and the read-only shell hook never lets such a line run without a prompt.

secretReads.description: A call that would print a secret: cat .env, Get-Content ~/.npmrc, the Read tool on a secret file, env, printenv, Get-ChildItem Env:, echo $GITHUB_TOKEN, kubectl get secret -o yaml, kubectl config view --raw, and a shell line that reads a saved credential out of the host's store, printed or not (gh auth token, git credential fill, CredRead): deny refuses it, ask asks the human, allow lets it run, which is the owner's call: check flags it (SECRET-GUARD-OFF).

writes.description: A call that holds a secret as text: a command line with one in it (curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <a token>"), or a Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit whose written text holds one outside a secret file (a token written into src/): deny refuses it, ask asks the human, allow lets it run, which is the owner's call: check flags it (SECRET-GUARD-OFF).

paths.description: The team's own secret files, read after the defaults (**/.env, **/.env.*, ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/**, ~/.aws/credentials, **/.kube/config, ~/.docker/config.json, **/.git-credentials, ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, ~/.claude/history.jsonl, **/.claude/settings.local.json, ~/.bash_history, ~/.zsh_history, **/PSReadLine/*_history.txt, **/*.pem, **/*.key, **/*.p12, **/*.pfx, **/*.jks, **/*.keystore, **/id_rsa, **/id_ecdsa, **/id_ed25519, **/*.tfstate, **/*.tfstate.backup; .env.example, .env.sample and ~/.ssh/*.pub stay readable). ~/ starts at home, a glob with no leading / or drive matches at any depth, and the last glob that matches a path decides: !glob keeps a path readable.

envNames.description: The team's own patterns for environment variables whose values are secrets, regular expressions over the name with case ignored, read after the defaults (TOKEN, SECRET, PASSW, PASS, CRED, AUTH except AUTHOR and an auth mechanism or source, PRIVATE, KEY, DSN, WEBHOOK, COOKIE, PAT, SALT, and a store's connection URL or string by its kind: DB_URL, DATABASE_URL, PG_URI, CACHE_URL, BROKER_URL, CONNECTION_STRING). A store named by its product is the team's to add. The last pattern that matches a name decides: !pattern keeps a variable printable.

commands.description: The team's own commands whose output is a secret whatever file or variable they name, regular expressions over a command's program and arguments with case ignored, read after the default (kubectl config view --raw). The last pattern that matches a command decides: !pattern lets it print.

redact.description: After a Bash, PowerShell, Read or Grep call runs, replace each secret its result holds (a token by its shape, a match of register.secretPatterns, the value of a secret variable) before the model and the transcript see it, and tell the session which kinds it held and the task filed to rotate each. false shows results whole; turning it off is the owner's call: check flags it (SECRET-GUARD-OFF).

dbWriteGuard.description: Asks before a Bash or PowerShell call writes to a database by hand: a SQL client (psql, mysql, mariadb, sqlite3, built in) or a program of the team's (programs) whose code writes, a Node script, node -e or stdin whose client of the team's (nodeClients) writes, a container or remote host running one (kubectl exec, docker exec, ssh), or a data script (entrypoints) run with its apply flag. A read stays silent. A team's lists only add: a missing or broken entry never switches a built-in off.

writes.description: A hand-run database write: deny refuses it, ask asks the human (or refuses with the move-on note under prompts.hookAsks: refuse), allow lets it run.

entrypoints.description: The team's data scripts that write only with an apply flag, so a dry run passes: the script's path, matched against the end of the path a line runs (scripts/backfill.ts), and the flags that make it write (--apply, or --apply=yes on the line).

path.description: The script's path, matched against the end of the path a line runs: scripts/backfill.ts.

applyFlags.description: The flags that make the script write, --apply or --apply=yes; a run without one is a dry run.

programs.description: The team's database programs, by name and the arguments each reads, read before the built-in SQL clients: document-shell (--eval code, -f files, a script file named as a word; document methods such as insertOne, deleteMany, drop, an aggregation's $out or $merge), key-value-cli (a command word such as SET or DEL, EVAL scripts, --eval files, stdin lines), sql-command (-c, -f, stdin), sql-execute (-e, stdin) or sql-database-file (a database file, then SQL; -cmd, stdin).

name.description: The program's name as a line runs it, no path: my-cli, tool.exe.

reads.description: The arguments it takes its code from, one of the shapes programs lists.

nodeClients.description: The Node client modules whose calls write, each with its vocabulary: document (insertOne, updateMany, deleteMany, drop, bulkWrite...) or key-value (set, del, hset, expire, flushall, eval...). Node code (node -e, a script file, stdin) is read only when it imports or requires one of them, or a module/sub path under it.

module.description: The package name code loads, store or @scope/store; a store/sub path under it counts too.

vocabulary.description: The write vocabulary of its calls: document or key-value.

clientReceivers.description: Words that mark a key-value client in Node code, matched in any case inside a receiver's name, added to the built-in client: a call named like a shared method (set, rename, copy, append, eval, move, restore, unlink) writes only on such a receiver (cache.set, not map.set).

commits.description: The small-commits rule: one logical change per commit; a commit over either bound needs a reason line.

maxLines.description: Changed non-test lines (added + deleted) a commit may carry without a reason line.

maxFiles.description: Changed non-test files a commit may carry without a reason line.

largeCommitTrailer.description: The key of the reason line, as in `Large-commit: <reason>`.

testPatterns.description: Regular expressions over /-separated paths; a file that matches one is a test and never counts.

sourcePatterns.description: Regular expressions over /-separated paths; a non-test file that matches one is source. A change of source with no test changed misses the self-merge gate (pushGuard.pushToProtected gated).

gate.description: A push to a protected branch: off ignores large commits, warn lists them when it asks the human, refuse refuses the push.

delivery.description: The delivery flow: teamrig queue runs one queued step on the host at a time, under the host lock, teamrig merge merges a branch into its repository's default branch, teamrig deploy deploys it and teamrig freeze holds deploys while a session measures; each step is recorded in the ledger.

dir.description: The delivery folder, which holds its ledger (ledger.jsonl); a relative path is in the team's folder. Unset: deploys in the state folder.

repos.description: The repositories whose branches teamrig merge merges into their default branch, by name.

mainCheckout.description: The repository's main checkout; a branch merges from any worktree of it. A relative path is in the team's folder.

deploysOnPush.description: The deploy targets a push to the default branch deploys by itself (a host that builds on push): deploy freezes on them hold the merge, and the push is recorded as their deploy.

dependencyGate.description: Refuse a branch (merge) or a pushed range (deploy) whose package files need a dependency install, so the main checkout node_modules, which its worktrees link to, never changes unreviewed; dependencyCheck clears one for merge, and with deploy.dependencyInstall for a deploy.

dependencyCheck.description: With dependencyGate, what clears a dependency change: a program and its arguments, run without a shell under the host lock with the base package-lock.json in the file TEAMRIG_BASELINE_LOCK names (unset when the base has none). teamrig merge runs it in the branch checkout after the rebase and before the push, the default branch its base; teamrig deploy in the main checkout after the pull, its old HEAD the base. Exit 0 lets the change go, anything else refuses it.

reviewGate.description: Hold a branch (merge) whose changed paths hit a review entry (teamrig's generic list and pushGuard.reviewPaths) until its reviewer approves it, or reviewCheck clears its check hits.

reviewCheck.description: With reviewGate, what a check hit runs: a program and its arguments, run without a shell under the host lock in the branch checkout after the rebase, with the base commit in TEAMRIG_REVIEW_BASE. Exit 0 clears the change, 3 holds it for the entry's reviewer with the findings it prints, anything else for that reviewer too. Unset: a check hit is held like an always one.

docsFolder.description: The project's docs folder, where decisionRecordGate finds its decisions folder. A relative path is in the repository; an absolute one may be outside it, such as a separate docs repository.

decisionRecordGate.description: Refuse a branch (merge) whose task (a branch named t<n>-...) has a design note (a .md file in its task folder named for a design, such as design.md or pr2-design.md) until the change adds or changes a decision record in docsFolder/decisions/, so a design decided in a session's notes lands in the repository in its own words. With a docs folder outside the repository, a record there that names the task clears it.

updateMainCheckout.description: After the push, fast-forward the main checkout to it: only a fast-forward, only on the default branch with no tracked changes.

worktreeFolder.description: The folder teamrig worktree add makes each new worktree in, one folder per branch named after it with each / as -. A relative path is in the main checkout.

worktreeSetup.description: What teamrig worktree add runs in a new worktree, such as a link to the main checkout node_modules: a program and its arguments, run without a shell, with the main checkout folder in TEAMRIG_MAIN_CHECKOUT. Anything but exit 0 leaves the worktree in place and fails the add. Unset: nothing runs.

merge.description: How teamrig merge merges a branch through the team's own flow, such as a pull request the forge merges. Unset: it pushes the branch to the default branch.

command.description: A program and its arguments, run without a shell in the branch checkout under the host lock after the rebase and the dependency check, with TEAMRIG_MERGE_BRANCH, TEAMRIG_MERGE_BASE (the default branch), TEAMRIG_MERGE_HEAD and TEAMRIG_SESSION set. Exit 0: the branch merged, which teamrig merge confirms on the remote; 75: it waits (say a pull request waits on its checks or review), and running teamrig merge again finishes it once it merges; anything else fails it. Its last output line is shown as the reason.

remote.description: The git remote whose default branch the command merges into: teamrig merge rebases onto it, confirms the merge on it and moves the local default branch to it. Set upstream where origin is a contributor's fork; the branch itself is pushed to and deleted from origin either way.

deploy.description: How teamrig deploy deploys what merged into the default branch, each command a program and its arguments run without a shell from the main checkout. Unset: the repository is not deployed.

targets.description: The deploy targets it deploys: deploy freezes on them hold it.

checks.description: Checks asked in order before the host lock and again under it; the first that does not pass holds the deploy. Exit 0 lets it go, 75 makes it wait, 2 refuses it; anything else, or no answer within checkTimeoutSeconds, makes it wait.

name.description: Names the check in a wait or refusal.

command.description: The check: a program and its arguments.

dependencyInstall.description: Installs a pulled range's dependency change (package-lock.json, or package.json fields an install reads), such as npm ci --ignore-scripts: run after the pull and the dependencyCheck, before afterPull. A failed install moves the main checkout back and runs again to restore its dependencies. With dependencyGate, a dependency change deploys only when this and dependencyCheck are set.

afterPull.description: Run in order after the pull, before command; one that fails ends the deploy before its command runs.

command.description: Deploys what the pull brought: exit 0 deployed (a stdout line no-deploy: nothing needed deploying), else failed. Its last stdout line is the ledger note.

queue.description: The host lock and the limits of one queued step.

lockPath.description: The host lock file every queued step takes; a relative path is in the team's folder. Unset: host.lock in the kit home, one lock for every team on the host.

lockTtlMinutes.description: A taken host lock lasts this many minutes; past it, or once its process is gone, another step takes it over.

maxRunMinutes.description: A queued step still running after this many minutes is killed with every process it started. At most lockTtlMinutes less 10.

smallMaxRunMinutes.description: A small step (queue --small) still running after this many minutes is killed the same way, so a hung one does not hold back the steps waiting for the lock; a longer step runs without --small. At most maxRunMinutes.

waitMinutes.description: A queued step is refused once its line for the host lock has not moved for this many minutes: no step ahead of it, holding the lock or sharing the host ended meanwhile.

memorySampleSeconds.description: While a queued step runs, its process tree's memory and the host's free memory are sampled this often, for its ledger record's peakTreeMb and lowFreeMb; 0 samples nothing.

memoryFloorMb.description: A queued step, a merge or a deploy starts only while the host keeps this many MB free besides those held for it and for the small steps sharing the host.

smallReserveMb.description: The MB held for a small step whose need is neither learned from its past runs in the ledger nor declared with --memory-mb.

heavyReserveMb.description: The least MB held for a heavy queued step, a merge or a deploy besides memoryFloorMb: it takes the host lock only while free memory covers both (at most half the host's RAM). A heavy step whose need, learned from its past runs in the ledger or declared with --memory-mb, is more holds that instead.

admission.description: How the host lock's line is ordered: pipeline lets the most urgent step in first (a p0 step at once, then by class turn, priority raised by agingMinutes waited, and arrival), with at most perSessionRunning steps of one session running and maxHeavyParallel heavy steps sharing the host at once, and is the default; serial keeps the line in arrival order with no cap and one heavy step at a time, for a team whose own deploy tool takes the lock file without first waiting for the shares to end.

agingMinutes.description: In pipeline admission, a waiting step's priority rises one level per this many minutes waited, never to p0; 0 ages nothing.

perSessionRunning.description: In pipeline admission, a session with this many steps running (the host lock or a share of the host) waits for one to end, and later steps pass it; 0 caps nothing.

maxHeavyParallel.description: In pipeline admission, at most this many heavy queued steps share the host at once, each let in only while the memory gate has room for it beside the steps already sharing it; a merge and a deploy still take the whole host, waiting for every share to end.

checkTimeoutSeconds.description: A deploy's check still running after this many seconds is stopped, and the deploy waits.

freezes.description: Deploy freezes (teamrig freeze), which hold deploys of their targets while a session measures them.

maxMinutes.description: A freeze lasts at most this many minutes.

stablePeriods.description: teamrig stable-periods: when a measurement of a deploy target is clean, between the deploys and queued steps that disturb it.

settleMinutes.description: A target measures cleanly this many minutes after a deploy reached it.

targetSettleMinutes.description: Per deploy target, its own settle minutes in place of settleMinutes; each a target some repository deploys.

assumedDeployMinutes.description: How long a deploy is taken to have run before its ledger.md line when the ledger has no record of its start.

minMinutes.description: The shortest stable period worth listing.

pollSeconds.description: A waiting step looks again after this many seconds; the first in line for the host lock every 2 at most.

maxMinutes.description: A deploy step (teamrig merge, deploy) waits this many minutes at most for deploy freezes and the host lock, then is refused; a wait in a line for the lock that keeps moving goes on past them.

schedule.description: When queued steps and deploys may start on the host.

resetBlackoutHours.description: No deploy (teamrig merge) starts from this many hours before the weekly token reset until the reset. Unset: no blackout.

queueCutoffUtc.description: No queued step starts on the host after this UTC time until midnight.

budget.description: The weekly token budget: the pace line the team is measured against and each session's daily part of it. Usage is in weighted tokens (W) read from the session transcripts, and in % of the week from the status line when there is one. The defaults only measure and show; nothing blocks or acts.

enabled.description: Turns on the live warning and the core rules' pacing sentence; teamrig budget shows usage either way. Unset in a team under another on its account: the team above's.

account.description: The Claude account the team's week is on: teams with the same account share one week and split its daily budget. Unset: the team above's, else the one account the teams on its Claude config dir name (the dir its sessions last started in), else that dir, since one config dir signs in one account. A team that names an account other than the team above's takes none of the keys of the account's week from it (enabled, accountLead, weeklyLimitW, subagentWeight, extraWPerUsd, reset, resets).

accountLead.description: The root team whose lead is the account's main lead: after each reset it splits the week among the account's root teams, each lead then splits its part among its own team and its child teams, and the main lead reports the split at the owner's first meeting after the reset. Unset: the team above's, in a team under another on its account; else the root team's own lead, which holds while the account has one root team. Set it in every root team's config once a second root team joins the account.

weeklyLimitW.description: The weekly limit in weighted tokens. Unset: the team above's, in a team under another on its account; else derived from the status line's weekly %.

subagentWeight.description: What one W of a subagent's transcript costs against the weekly limit, in W of a main session. The meter multiplies each subagent call's W by it, so weeklyLimitW is in main-session W. 1: both cost alike. Unset in a team under another on its account: the team above's.

extraWPerUsd.description: W per US dollar of extra usage, standing in until two spent readings past 100% of the week teach the rate. Unset: the team above's, in a team under another on its account; else the extra-usage pool shows in dollars only until then, with no allowance.

reset.description: When the weekly limit resets, for a team without a status line. Unset: the team above's, in a team under another on its account; else the reset time the status line reports.

weekday.description: The day the weekly limit resets.

timeUtc.description: The time it resets, HH:MM UTC.

resets.description: The resets the account holds beside its weekly one, each grant with its expiry and the uses taken from it; Claude Code does not tell a session about them, so the team writes them down as they are granted and used. teamrig budget shows what is left of each. Unset: the team above's, in a team under another on its account; else none.

kind.description: fable refills the Fable bar and gives back what Fable used of the weekly limit; full clears all of the week's usage.

count.description: How many resets the grant holds.

expiresUtc.description: When the grant's unused resets expire, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC.

usedUtc.description: When each use was taken, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC; at most count. Unset: none used.

note.description: One short line about the grant, such as where it came from.

targetPct.description: Use the week up to this share of the weekly limit.

reservePct.description: Kept back for incidents until shortly before the reset; targetPct plus reservePct is at most 100.

shareFloorPct.description: The least share of each weekly split a team with planned work gets, in % of the part being split; when the floors do not fit, each team gets an equal part. 0: no floor. The team's own, never taken from the team above. The lead's rules print it while the budget is enabled.

paceEndHoursBeforeReset.description: The pace line reaches targetPct this many hours before the reset.

sessions.description: Each session's weight in the split of the team's daily budget, by id: its part is the budget × share × its top queued task's weight (by priority, however many tasks it has queued) / the sum over the sessions, recomputed at every reading. A session not listed has a share of 1.

share.description: The session's weight in the split, as sessions describes it.

pauseByPriority.description: On a short day, when what is left of the week gives less than the pace line plans for the day, fund the team's sessions in the priority order of their top queued task (p0 first, idle sessions last) and pause the sessions none of it reaches, so the top work keeps its pace. The lead, the delivery owner held in the team and lifted sessions are never paused. Off: no session of the team is paused.

warnAtPct.description: The live warning shows a line as a session passes each of these % of its daily budget.

fiveHourWarnPct.description: The five-hour check warns the lead once the account's five-hour window reaches this %; a rise forecast to fill the window warns sooner. Only a plan whose status line reports the window is warned: on any other nothing is read or shown.

paceTolerancePct.description: The team is ahead of its pace line once its used % is more than this many points above it.

overAction.description: Past a session's daily budget: warn shows the lines only; ask-lead also writes the lead an inbox line; ask also asks the person before a helper launch; block refuses helper launches.

escalate.description: When an action beyond the lines applies: session when the session is over its budget; session-and-fleet only when the team is also ahead of its pace line.

quietHours.description: UTC hours in which the live warning applies action on its own, while the team sleeps. Unset: none.

startUtc.description: Where the quiet hours start, HH:MM UTC.

endUtc.description: Where they end, HH:MM UTC; an end before the start runs them past midnight.

action.description: What the live warning does in the quiet hours, with overAction's choices. ask holds a helper launch on a permission prompt that nobody at the host answers at night, so its tab stalls until someone does (teamrig doctor flags it); block refuses the launch with its reason and the tab goes on.

paceWeight.description: What a quiet minute counts on the pace line and in the daily budget, against 1 for any other minute. 0 when unset: the team sleeps, so the line stays flat through the night.

lift.description: Bounds on a leader's lift of a session's or a sub-lead's group's daily budget (teamrig budget lift). Every lift carries a stop %, the share of the week at which it ends.

maxStopPct.description: The highest stop % a lift may carry.

reserveStopPct.description: The highest stop % of a --reserve lift, given only in the last hour before the reset; it ends 15 minutes before the reset. Never below maxStopPct.

statusSnapshotDir.description: The folder of status line snapshots, <Claude session id>.json each. Unset: <kit home>/usage/live.

maxBytesPerHook.description: The most transcript bytes one hook run reads; the rest waits for the next run.

leadBoundary.description: How teamrig keeps the lead leading: its own edits, tests and code searches are nudged and shown, never blocked.

enabled.description: Off: the lead's own edits, tests and code searches are neither nudged nor shown.

ownPaths.description: The lead's own files and folders beyond the team's teamrig folder and Claude Code's memory folders, which always count: editing or searching them is its job. ~ is the user's home, * one folder name.

searchNudgeAt.description: The turn's code search (a source-file Read, a Grep, a Glob or a shell search outside the lead's own paths) that brings the lead one nudge, and from which the owner's turn-end line counts searches; 0 never.

chainNudgeAt.description: After this many single-tool calls in a row in one turn, the session gets one line asking it to send independent steps as several tool calls in one message, and an edit with its re-test; 0 never asks.

wake.description: Waking a session idle at its prompt when work is handed to it, instead of at its next prompt. Only work the session can go on with wakes (open or started past every task it comes after, or waiting with every wait cleared or answered), tasks handed together wake once, and each wake says what it costs.

enabled.description: Off: a session sees new work only at its next prompt.

priority.description: The least urgent priority that wakes a session: 1 wakes for p0 and p1 only. A session its budget holds (past its daily budget while the team has no room today, the wake's own turn counted for both) or a short day pauses (`budget.pauseByPriority`) wakes for p0 only, and one in the budget's quiet hours for p0 and p1 only (p0 alone when their action is block), whatever this says.

batchSeconds.description: How long a wake waits after the first new task it is for, so tasks handed together wake the session once.

minGapMinutes.description: The least time between two wakes of one session; work handed meanwhile waits and wakes it once.

dayStartUtc.description: The day's start (HH:MM UTC, outside the budget's quiet hours): from then each session with work it can start, of any priority, that has had no turn since gets one wake that day, and a burst wakes its sessions the same way once it starts. Unset: no day-start wake, and a burst wakes no one.

tests.description: What teamrig test prints of a failed run.

maxFailureChars.description: The most characters of failing tests teamrig test prints after a failed run, all of them together; the rest stays in its log.

github.description: The team's GitHub repositories. teamrig gh sync reads their issues into the register as tasks of source github, and never writes to GitHub; local tasks stay local. teamrig gh migrate, teamrig issue comment and teamrig issue close, run by hand, write only to these repositories. Each owner's repositories are reached with the token saved as teamrig-gh-<owner> in the system's credential store, else the gh login; a saved token that cannot be read stops a write, never the gh login in its place (docs/github-sync.md).

repos.description: The repositories to read, as owner/name; matched without case. Empty turns the import off.

owners.description: The session that owns an issue assigned to each GitHub login; matched without case. An issue with no listed assignee goes to its repository's session in sessions, else the lead.

sessions.description: The session that owns the issues of each repository (owner/name, one of repos; matched without case) when none of their assignees is in owners. Without one, they go to the lead.

closedDays.description: How many days back closed issues are read, to finish the tasks they were imported as.

everyMinutes.description: How often the hooks start a sync on their own, in minutes, once for the whole team; 0 leaves it to teamrig gh sync --yes.

similarThreshold.description: The score, from 0 to 1, at which a mirrored issue counts as a duplicate candidate of a new one: the cosine of their TF-IDF word vectors. Higher lists fewer, closer candidates.

acceptLabel.description: The label that lets an issue by an author outside the repository (not its owner, an organization member or a collaborator) become a task: it counts when someone other than the author added it last and the title and body were not edited after that. Matched without case.

alerts.description: The alerting rule the core rules state, and where a page to the owner goes.

persistentFailureHours.description: The same external failure for this long must page a human.

pageWebhookEnv.description: The name of the environment variable holding the chat webhook URL that a page to the owner (an expired Claude login) is posted to, never the URL itself. Unset, with pageWebhookFile unset too: nothing pages.

pageWebhookFile.description: The absolute path of a file holding that webhook URL as its first non-empty line, or as the value of pageWebhookKey's key, read at each page, so the URL never sits in an environment, a log or a session's read. Wins over pageWebhookEnv when both are set. A URL that is not https pages no one.

pageWebhookKey.description: With pageWebhookFile: the key whose value in that file is the webhook URL, on a line `<key>: <value>` or `<key>=<value>` (a YAML map such as a Kubernetes secret's stringData, or a .env file), the value bare or in quotes. So a secrets file holding many keys is read in place, and the URL keeps one home. Unset: the file's first non-empty line is the URL.

decisions.description: When the lead asks the owner the decisions waiting on them (tasks waiting on the owner's decision or approval), together in one batch instead of one at a time. A batch holds the waits not yet asked and the asked ones now past their due date; `teamrig decisions` prints it and `teamrig decisions asked` records it asked, as a meeting's start does. The lead's check says when one is due.

batchTimesUtc.description: The lead's batch times, HH:MM UTC (its budget checkpoints, say): a batch is due once one passed since the last was asked. A wait due before the next batch time is asked at once. With none, a batch comes only at the daily meeting or by batchAt, and a wait due within a day is asked at once.

batchAt.description: A batch is due once this many waits on the owner are not yet asked; 0: never by count.

dedicatedOwners.description: Sessions that own the team's core-business areas. The owner never decides their waits from a daily card or a batch: the meeting agenda lists them under DEDICATED, by owning session, with the lines that ask that session for a full brief and book its own meeting after the daily (meeting schedule).

tabStatus.description: A colored circle before each terminal tab's title for what its session is doing: green ready, yellow working (or a helper still running), orange waiting on the user, blue waiting on the user's decision (a turn whose last message has a `Decision needed:` line), red an API error, purple compacting.

enabled.description: Shows the circle in every tab of the team; team create turns it on in a new team's config. It also needs CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 in Claude Code's environment, else Claude Code writes its own title over it.

needsYou.description: The needs-you band: every tab of the team shows which other tab asks the user something (a permission prompt, a question, a `Decision needed:` line), read from the tab files under state/tabs/, with a Focus button that brings that tab to the front. During an open meeting only a p0 task's ask gets the Focus button.

enabled.description: Off: no tab shows another's asks. The tab files are still written, for smart focus.

kinds.description: The kinds of ask that raise the band and its toast: permission (a permission prompt), question (AskUserQuestion or a plan to approve), elicitation (an MCP server's form), decision (a turn ending on a `Decision needed:` line), error (an API error).

osToast.description: Also one OS notification per ask across the team, besides the toast in each tab; it has no click action.

pickerGuard.description: Refuses Claude Code's question picker (AskUserQuestion) in every session and helper of the team, the lead's own thread included, in the owner's daily meeting too, where the lead asks each card in plain text: the picker stops the session until the person answers, and the owner may be away for hours, so none of its other tasks moves meanwhile. The refusal tells the session to decide it when it is its own, else to record it on its task (a waiting status with its decision card, --default included), which reaches the owner through the lead, and go on with its next task; only with no task left, to end its turn with the question and a `Decision needed:` line. A helper ends its report with the decision instead. Plan mode's ExitPlanMode stays allowed.

enabled.description: Refuses the question picker in every session and helper of the team, the lead's own thread included, in the owner's daily meeting too. On unless a team sets it false.

meeting.description: The owner's daily meeting with the lead, in the lead's tab.

panel.description: The agenda panel beside the lead's chat while a meeting is open.

enabled.description: Shows the panel in the lead's tab while a meeting is open: the owner's cards in the agenda's order, the ones decided since the meeting started checked off with the decision, the card on the table now marked. No other tab shows it. On unless a team sets it false.

spotlight.description: The spotlight while a meeting is open: every screen dimmed but the window holding the lead's tab. Windows Terminal on Windows only.

enabled.description: Starts the spotlight when meeting start opens the owner's daily meeting; it lifts by itself within seconds of meeting end, or when the meeting lapses. The dimming lets every click through and never takes the focus. On unless a team sets it false.

dim.description: How dark the rest of the screen goes, as the dimming layer's opacity: 0.1 barely shades it, 0.9 nearly hides it.

breakthroughSeconds.description: How long the dimming lifts when a CRITICAL message from another session breaks through the meeting hold to the lead, so the owner sees it at once; the dimming comes back by itself after that.

statusLine.description: The status line while a meeting is open: the lead's tab shows its line in the meeting colour, every other tab adds the held text, so a glance at any tab tells the meeting is on.

enabled.description: Marks the status lines while the owner's daily meeting is open; they go back as they were at meeting end, or when the meeting lapses. On unless a team sets it false.

colour.description: The lead's status line colour while a meeting is open, as #rrggbb; the terminal must show 24-bit colour.

heldText.description: The words every other tab's status line adds while a meeting is open, on one line.

turnLog.description: Each session's prompts and replies, kept in state/turn-log/<session>/<UTC hour>.jsonl for the task pane, so a /clear or a compaction never takes away what the person was reading in the tab. Secret shapes are redacted.

keepHours.description: How long each entry is kept, in hours; whole hours past it are removed at a session start.

meetingNotices.description: What a booked meeting (teamrig meeting schedule) tells the person, and when: a notice some minutes before its slot, one at the slot, and an alert once it is some minutes past its slot with no meeting start. Each notice goes out once, by whichever tab of the team looks first, on each channel left on.

enabled.description: Off: no meeting notice of any kind.

beforeMinutes.description: The early notice, in minutes before the slot; 0: none.

atStart.description: The notice at the slot's time.

missedAfterMinutes.description: The missed alert, in minutes past the slot's time with no meeting start; 0: none.

osToast.description: The operating system's notification: a toast on Windows, a banner on macOS, notify-send on Linux.

tabToast.description: A toast in the open tab of the team that sends the notice; a missed alert's stays a minute, the longest Claude Code shows one.

leadInbox.description: One inbox line to the team's lead for a missed meeting.

readonlyShell.description: Lets a Bash or PowerShell line run without a permission prompt when every command in it provably only reads: known readers (grep, cat, Get-Content, Select-Object...), git and kubectl reading subcommands, and no write, file redirection, command that runs code, or variable a program reads. It only ever allows: any other line gets Claude Code's own permission check.

enabled.description: Turns the hook on for every session of the team.

allowPrefixes.description: Commands trusted with any arguments, each by its leading words, such as "npx tsc --noEmit" or "npx jest". The hook cannot read what they do, so a prefix vouches for every argument after it: leave out a tool whose flags write (eslint --fix, jest -u).

permissions.description: Which local allow rules stay. An allow rule in a Claude Code settings file approves a call before auto mode's classifier sees it, so a rule that approves a whole tool or a program with any arguments skips the one check that stops an injected or mistaken action. teamrig permissions trim removes the rules off keepAllow (the owner runs it with --yes); doctor flags the ones that approve a whole tool or program, or hold a credential (text in a secret's shape) that Claude Code saved with an approved command.

keepAllow.description: Rules kept as they are, such as "Bash(kubectl get *)" or "WebSearch": a tool, or a tool and a command with at most a trailing " *" or ":*" (read as the same). A kept "Tool(x *)" also keeps "Tool(x)", and a shell rule's leading "MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 " reads as absent. Keep only commands whose arguments can neither run a program nor write. The default is the general part of security's list of read-only commands outside Claude Code's own read-only set; a team's list replaces it, so one that adds its own tools' read-only commands repeats the default's.

open.description: How teamrig open starts a session in a new terminal tab.

terminal.description: The terminal to open the tab in. auto takes tmux inside tmux, else Windows Terminal on Windows, Terminal on macOS, or the first of gnome-terminal, konsole and x-terminal-emulator on Linux; print opens nothing and prints the command to run. teamrig open --terminal wins over it.

teamWindow.description: Opens each tab of the team's sessions (teamrig open, a meeting start, a refresh restart, the idle pass's reopen and a restore after a reboot) in a Windows Terminal window of the team's own, named teamrig-<team>, made when none is open, so each team's tabs stay apart from other teams'. Off opens them in the most recent window. Other terminals open as before.

headroom.description: The room teamrig open and teamrig hire --yes need on the host before they add a session: free memory over floorMb with the session and the tabs still loading counted, and the commit charge within commitMaxPct. One tab is admitted at a time on the host, for every team. The lead opens whatever the room.

sessionMb.description: The MB a new session is counted to need while no session runs to measure; else the median running session's Claude Code process tree.

commitMaxPct.description: The most of the host's commit limit, in %, its commit charge may reach with the new session counted (Windows, and Linux under strict overcommit, vm.overcommit_memory 2; elsewhere free memory alone is checked).

closeIdleMinutes.description: How long, in minutes, a session stays quiet before teamrig close may end it to free the host; teamrig open resumes it.

floorMb.description: The MB free memory must keep with a new tab and the tabs still loading counted. Unset: delivery.queue.memoryFloorMb plus delivery.queue.heavyReserveMb, so a new tab leaves room for one heavy queued step.

loadMinutes.description: How long, in minutes, a tab just opened holds the MB it was counted at, while it loads and free memory does not show it yet. Tab opens and queued steps on the host count the held MB as taken.

idle.description: The idle pass: it would close a session the wake check would not wake once it has been quiet open.headroom.closeIdleMinutes, and reopen it when the wake check would wake it. The lead and the delivery owner are never closed.

mode.description: off runs no pass; dry-run runs it and logs each close or reopen it would make, with its reason, and makes none; on, the default, also starts each of those closes and reopens, hidden, and logs its outcome.

keepOpen.description: Sessions the idle pass and teamrig close never close for being quiet, on top of the lead and the delivery owner.

statusLine.description: What teamrig statusline shows beside the model and the plan's use of the week.

folder.description: The name of the session's folder.

branch.description: The branch checked out there, or the commit of a detached HEAD.

pace.description: Where the team's pace line stands now, beside the week's use, as in week 63% (pace 53%): the line teamrig budget reads, from the week's start, after a reset inside the week from that reset, by the team's budget.targetPct, budget.paceEndHoursBeforeReset and budget.quietHours. Outside a team, none.

focus.description: Goal-first ranking: the work classes a task is filed under (teamrig add and update --class), how its WSJF score is made (cost of delay over size), the WIP rule and the share of the week each class is planned to take. When classes, roadmapClass, maintenanceClass, defaultClass and allocation disagree, each problem is reported and all five take their defaults.

classes.description: The classes --class takes: 1 to 12 names, each once, a letter then up to 31 letters, digits, spaces, _ or -.

roadmapClass.description: The class ranked by its goals' rank, which the WIP rule protects: one of classes.

maintenanceClass.description: The class ranked by severity first (bug, critical): one of classes.

defaultClass.description: The class a task with none counts as; it ranks last. One of classes.

maxActiveKeyResults.description: The key results (goals with a parent) the team may hold with a target of today or later; teamrig goal add refuses one more.

slicesPerSession.description: The shippable slices (a goal's fewest tasks that ship something working, proven live) each session keeps open at once; one more opens only while one waits on another session or the owner. Other work waits, incidents and Maintenance excepted. Replaces maxOpenSlices, a cap across the tree a lead could fill with its own team's slices. The lead's rules print it.

maxOwnerDecisions.description: The owner decisions that may wait at once across the root team's tree: a slice whose next step needs a new one does not open while this many wait. Each lead's rules print its own team's value, so set the same one in every team of a tree.

score.description: The parts of a task's WSJF score: cost of delay (value + urgency + unblocks + owner order) over size, in % of the week.

rankValues.description: The value of a Roadmap task whose best goal rank (on its goals or their parents) is 1, 2 and so on; a rank past the list takes the last.

roadmapUnranked.description: The value of a Roadmap task that serves no ranked goal.

maintenanceValue.description: The value of a Maintenance task, before its bug and critical additions.

maintenanceBug.description: Added to the value of a Maintenance task of type bug.

maintenanceCritical.description: Added to the value of a Maintenance task marked critical.

improvementsValue.description: The value of an Improvements task, and of a task with no class.

overdueValue.description: The urgency of a task past its due.

dueSoonValue.description: The urgency of a task due within dueSoonDays.

dueSoonDays.description: How many days before its due a task counts as due soon.

unblocksShare.description: The share of the best value among the active tasks that need a task (by after or a task wait) added to its own cost of delay; 0 turns it off.

ownerOrderValues.description: What an owner-sourced task's priority p1, p2 and so on adds, a capped override; the priorities of other tasks add nothing.

defaultSizePct.description: The size, in % of the week, of a task with no size, no spend and no like tasks finished to measure by.

minSizePct.description: The smallest size, in % of the week, a score divides by, so a tiny task cannot outrank everything.

expedite.description: Which tasks go ahead of every score, beside a p0, which always does.

wip.description: The WIP rule: an Improvements start is held while its owner has a Roadmap task that can move, or until the week resets once Improvements has spent its allocation, and a start past maxInProgress is held. --one-commit, a reopen of a verifying or done task, an expedited task and an owner-sourced task are exempt.

mode.description: refuse holds the start; warn prints why and lets it through; off checks nothing.

maxInProgress.description: The in-progress tasks a session may hold before a further start is held.

allocation.description: The % of the whole week each class is planned to take, by class; every key one of classes, the shares summing to 100. A class outside roadmapClass and maintenanceClass that reaches its share has its starts held until the week resets, unless wip's mode is off; a class left out is never held, and one at 0 is held from the week's start.

additionalProperties.description: The class's share of the whole week, in %.

leaderWaitMinutes.description: How long, in minutes, a Roadmap task may wait on a leader's decision or approval before it is flagged.

parkAfterDays.description: The days without an event after which an Improvements task is parked out of list, plan, check and start; any update brings it back.

plannedTargetPct.description: The % of the week's spend planned work should take.

improvementsDay.description: The UTC weekday whose meeting agenda carries the Improvements decisions, as one batch; the default is the first meeting of the plan week, and no other day's agenda shows them.

launch.description: Each session's Claude Code model and effort, and the folder it works in, by id: teamrig open starts it with claude --model and --effort; a session running on another model is told the /model to type at its start, and one at another effort the /effort to type at its first stop. A model or effort left unset is Claude Code's own choice, except for the lead, which starts on model opus at xhigh effort for each one it leaves unset.

model.description: A Claude Code model alias or a full model id such as claude-opus-5-5. best is Fable where the account has it, else Opus; default leaves the model to Claude Code.

effort.description: The effort level; a model that lacks it runs at the highest level it has below it. An /effort the user types in the session's tab is written here.

project.description: The session's project folder, an absolute path: teamrig open starts it there, and close and hire look for its Claude Code sessions there. Unset, team.project, else the folder holding the team's .teamrig.json pointer; doctor flags a folder that does not exist.

refresh.description: Context refresh: when a session finishes a task (teamrig set <id> --status done) with its context at or over contextTokens, or with everyTasks tasks finished since its context was last fresh and the context at everyTasksMinTokens or more, or after the lead ran teamrig refresh <session>, it writes a handover; then the user types /clear, or teamrig starts it fresh on its own (autoRestart). A relative handoverDir is resolved against the team's folder; unset, it is <team folder>/handover.

enabled.description: Off: no session is asked for a handover or refreshed.

contextTokens.description: The context size, in tokens, that asks for a refresh: under the about 167k where Claude Code compacts a 200k window.

everyTasks.description: Also refresh once this many tasks were finished since the context was last fresh (a /clear, a new process or a compaction); 0 turns it off.

everyTasksMinTokens.description: The smallest context, in tokens, the task count refreshes at.

tabTitle.description: Title the tab once the handover is written: '[<team>] <name>: restarting', or '[<team>] <name>: type /clear'.

autoRestart.description: Once the handover is written and the turn has ended, start the session fresh on its own, which reads the handover: the plugin's mod runs /clear in its tab; where no mod claims the ask, teamrig ends its Claude Code and starts it again, in the same tab when teamrig open started it, else in a new tab. A session with no work it can start then waits for a wake that brings it some, which starts it fresh instead of waking it. A prompt typed before then keeps the context. false (the default): the user types /clear once done with the screen, which a /clear wipes.

restartDelaySeconds.description: How long after the turn's end the automatic restart waits, so the user can still type to keep the context.

holdAfterActivityMinutes.description: The plugin's mod holds the automatic /clear while the person typed in the tab's prompt (a key, a paste) or sent a prompt there this recently, and while the prompt holds a draft: a /clear never lands under the person. The default 30 min keeps the context through the person's talk in the tab (reading a reply, thinking it over), the restart coming once they have been away that long. 0: only a draft holds it.

countdownSeconds.description: Before the plugin's mod runs the automatic /clear, a band above the prompt counts down this many seconds, with Refresh now and Hold 10 min; a key in the prompt holds it too. 0: no count, the /clear runs once nothing else holds it.

compactCeilingTokens.description: While a session's handover is asked for or written, the plugin's mod stops Claude Code's own compaction (trigger auto) of its main conversation as long as its context, as Claude Code estimates it, is under this many tokens: the /clear at the turn's end replaces it. Where a managed mod runs first and sends the compaction on past the plugin's mod, the classic PreCompact hook stops it instead, on the context it estimates from the transcript and a 200,000-token window. Past it a compaction goes through; /compact and a subagent's own compaction are never stopped. 0: never stopped. It also bounds an open owner meeting (the lead's daily one, or a booked one from its meeting start M<n>), which holds the refresh of each session in it only under it; 0 holds it until the meeting ends.

handoverMaxBytes.description: The turn end (and teamrig refresh --ready) takes no handover larger than this many bytes: the fresh start reads all of it, so a handover that grows section by section fills the next session's context before its work begins. 0: no cap.

endCommand.description: A program (its path, then its arguments) run after an automatic restart ended a session, given Claude Code's SessionEnd hook input (reason clear) on stdin: for a SessionEnd hook the end skipped, since on Windows a process is ended without running them. Empty: none.

handoverDir.description: The folder of the sessions' handovers, <session>.md each; a relative path is in the team's folder. Unset: handover in the team's folder.

hiring.description: Hiring sessions with teamrig hire, each a worker the leader is sure the team needs: who decides. No cap counts hires: the host's room bounds who is at the office, and the leader decides who is hired. A hire is written into sessions, names and launch, and logged with its reason and review date; its part of the team's daily budget follows its share and queued work, like any session's.

policy.description: off: no hires. owner: a lead (the lead, or a sub-lead into its own group) hires once the owner approved (--approved-by, kept with the hire). lead: a lead hires. automatic: as lead, and a hired session whose last open task closes is asked to write its handover. Under every policy only a lead over a session retires it (teamrig retire).

reviewDays.description: Days from a hire to its review date, unless teamrig hire --review names one.

resumeMaxTokens.description: The most context tokens a rehired session's last Claude Code session may hold for teamrig open --resume to resume it; past it the session starts fresh on its handover.

resumeMaxIdleDays.description: The most days a rehired session's last Claude Code session may have gone unwritten for teamrig open --resume to resume it; past it the session starts fresh on its handover.

scaleOut.description: How teamrig check measures an area against its dated work for a SCALE-OUT flag: its pace is the tasks it finished lately, and the dated tasks of the top priorities are what it must finish in time.

windowDays.description: Days back over which the tasks an area finished give its pace; at most the 8 days a register keeps finished tasks.

minDone.description: The fewest tasks an area must have finished in that window for its pace to count; below it the area is not measured.

topPriorities.description: How many of the top priorities count: their dated tasks are the work an area must finish in time.

burst.description: Bursts with teamrig burst: a time-boxed scale-out onto helpers and hired sessions that spends more of the week, for a surplus the week would leave unused at the reset or for a deadline. A person always starts one by command; nothing starts one on its own.

policy.description: off: no bursts. owner: the lead starts one once the owner approved (--approved-by, kept with the burst). lead: the lead starts one within the caps.

surplusHours.description: A surplus burst starts at the earliest this many hours before the week's reset.

minSparePct.description: The least share of the week, in %, projected unused at the pace end (at the week's mean rate so far) for a surplus burst; with other teams on the Claude account, the team's part of it (split by weight, as the daily budget is).

maxHelpers.description: The most helpers each burst session runs at once; the burst's model line states it.

maxHires.description: The most sessions one burst may hire (teamrig hire --burst).

paths.description: Folders moved from their defaults; a relative path is resolved against the team's folder (<kit home>/teams/<team>). Unset, state and inbox stay under the team's folder and skills is the skills folder of Claude Code's folder ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.claude).

state.description: The team's state folder: the task list's log, the inboxes, the delivery ledger and the logs. Unset: state in the team's folder.

inbox.description: The folder of the sessions' inbox files. Unset: inbox in the state folder.

skills.description: The Claude Code skills folder teamrig check and doctor read. Unset: skills in Claude Code's folder ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.claude).

roleHolder.description: A session of the team by id, or `<team>/<id>`: the session holding the same role on a team above it (doctor's tree-role problem when that team is not above, or the session does not hold the role there).
